limitations: DID B does not exist. This manifest records an enrollment design and a custody-capability finding, not a second enrolled identity.

The custody primitives (DPAPIKeyProvider, TrustedPaths.under, canonical_did) accept any state root and were proved isolated using throwaway fixture keys. The shipped enrollment CLI local_init.main() pins the state root to %LOCALAPPDATA%\TechnocoreAgent and refuses any other root.

The operator declined to bypass that CLI guard by invoking initialize_local_identity() directly. There is therefore no reviewed production path to enrol a second identity, and Phase 3B.C1 stops before creating DID B.
Role assignment is frozen as a design decision only. Neither role is bound to a key, because only one identity exists.

Two distinct DIDs would prove cryptographic role separation only. They would remain ONE human operator: not two humans, not two organizations, not two economic counterparties, not two wallet owners, not evidence of payment, and not FLOP eligibility.
The fixture isolation probe used real Windows DPAPI but disposable keys with no operator credential. It demonstrates namespace separation, not that an enrolled second identity is safe to operate.
No signature was produced for any identity in this phase. A DID is derived from public-key material only; possession of a working signing path for DID B is unproven and belongs to a later phase.
reviewedEnrollmentEntrypointRequirements: reuse the existing DPAPIKeyProvider and initialize_local_identity primitives without modification
leave the default canonical identity path and its single-root guard intact
require an explicit named identity/profile argument
constrain the storage root to a reviewed namespace under %LOCALAPPDATA%
refuse path traversal and arbitrary filesystem roots
refuse to write into or adjacent to an existing identity's files
never expose the passphrase or private key to Cline or Node
perform no signing, nonce reservation, transport, or network activity
nextRecommendedAction: Phase 3B.C1a — review and land a narrow, human-only multi-identity enrollment entrypoint in canonical, then re-run Phase 3B.C1 to enrol DID B
